pages.text: Replace the electron and chemistry changes. A $(thing)positron$() makes positronium - an atom of matter and antimatter - and $(item)Positronium Hydride$() is a molecule of it. A $(thing)muon$() is 200 times heavier than an electron, so a $(item)Muonic Catalyst$() squeezes atoms close enough to fuse cold.
A $(item)Room-Temperature Superconductor$() - hydrogen packed into a framework - carries current with zero resistance and no cryogenics.
A molecule made of a hydrogen atom and an atom of matter bound to antimatter. It lasts a nanosecond - unless you trap it.$(br2)Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().
Swap an electron for a muon and atoms shrink 200 times - close enough to fuse cold.$(br2)Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().
Zero resistance without cryogenics. Physicists have chased this for a century.$(br2)Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().
